solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Kind of box that's kept without its top facing up?

indicators.note: the box holds something within it, so the second piece is kept inside the first

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box for goods
preceded by 'without', this describes a box that is not upright, so lying on one face

explanation.surface: A riddle about some sort of box stored with its lid turned away from the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like 'sort of', leading into the box, but it is the definition. A box kept 'without its top facing up' is lying ON SIDE, and the CRATE keeps that inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone thoughtful and caring towards other people; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Celebrations in verse? Ways to put maiden off!

indicators.note: together with off, this tells us a letter is put away from the word
off completes the instruction to remove the letter

parts.note: modes are ways or manners of doing things
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Poems of praise are a way to deter a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed in praise of a subject are celebrations written in verse.

clue.text: Stir created by one leaping into crowd

definitions.meaning: a slam dancer hurls themselves into the crowd at a rock gig

explanation.surface: A commotion caused by someone jumping into a throng.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like a commotion but is prison slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Both stir and this word are slang for jail; it is also a slam dancer or stage diver.

clue.text: Famous expert on cancer offers model

definitions.meaning: Sir Richard ..., the epidemiologist who linked smoking to lung cancer
a figure of a person made as a toy

explanation.surface: A renowned oncologist poses as a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Richard Doll proved smoking causes lung cancer; a toy figure of a person is also called this.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of order, not the first I received

indicators.note: the letter I is taken in by the shortened word
this drops the opening letter of the order

parts.note: a precept is a command or rule of conduct

explanation.surface: Confirmation of a purchase order, though not the first one I got.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acknowledgement of order' reads as one phrase, but 'order' is the start of the wordplay: PRECEPT less P, taking in I.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is a written note confirming that payment or goods have been received.

clue.text: Some exceptional eating — up will go that weight!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
some means only part of the run of words is used

explanation.surface: A spot of exceptional feasting, and your weight will rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A tael is an old Far Eastern unit of weight, also used for silver money.

clue.text: Ardent President once giving sign to prophet

parts.note: ardent literally means burning, from the Latin ardere
Bush is the surname of two former US presidents

explanation.surface: A passionate former president sends a signal to a seer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus God speaks to Moses from a bush that burns without being consumed.

clue.text: Drug cupboard — guess sailor will go to that

indicators.note: the guess and the sailor are placed before the cupboard, going to it

parts.note: to bet is to wager on a guess
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
a locker is a small lockable cupboard

explanation.surface: A sailor is guessing what is inside a medicine cupboard and heading over to check.
explanation.definitionFit: A beta blocker is a class of medication used to slow the heart and lower blood pressure.

clue.text: Indication of illegitimacy given by arbiters troubled about offence

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit around the offence
troubled letters are disturbed, so they are mixed into a new order

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence

explanation.surface: Judges in turmoil over a wrongdoing reveal someone born out of wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagonal band on a coat of arms was popularly held to signify a bastard line in heraldry.

clue.text: Awe-inspiring fortification on island to the north

parts.note: a redoubt is a small outlying fort

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading upwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: An impressive stronghold stands on an island in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Formidable and worthy of fear or respect; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Two lots of soldiers going to party, with loss of concentration

parts.note: RA (Royal Artillery) and RE (Royal Engineers) are two British army units
a faction is a group or party within a larger body

explanation.surface: Troops arrive at a celebration and everyone's focus slips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concentration' suggests attention, but it is density in the physics sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarefaction is the thinning of a gas or medium, reducing its density.

clue.text: What is poisonous, completely? Arsenic

parts.note: up means completely, as in 'eat it up' or 'time is up'
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: A question about what counts as utterly toxic, with arsenic as the obvious reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a tropical Asian tree whose sap was used as arrow poison, famed as poisonous.

clue.text: Mythological female in terrible danger

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words terrible danger

explanation.surface: A woman from legend finds herself in dreadful peril.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was the queen of Sparta whom Zeus seduced in the form of a swan.

clue.text: Swiss company had finally got into a comfortable position

parts.note: Nestlé is the food and drinks company based in Switzerland

indicators.note: finally picks out the end letter of the word had

explanation.surface: A Swiss firm has at last settled into a secure place in the market.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle snugly, so having nestled means having settled cosily.

clue.text: Block to keep water back? That would be mad

parts.note: the word dam written upwards, as a down light reads, gives mad

explanation.surface: Building a barrier against the water would be a crazy idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To dam up a river is to block its flow with a barrier, holding the water back.

clue.text: One sip's disastrous — it's spiked!

indicators.note: a disastrous outcome is a wreck, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a single sip is a disaster because the drink has been laced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiked' reads as a doctored drink, but it means having spines.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinose is a botanical and zoological term for covered in spines, that is, prickly.

clue.text: Carpenter unusually had same experience as cat in London?

parts.note: in the rhyme Pussycat, Pussycat, the cat went to London and saw the Queen
the Queen the cat met in London is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A craftsman, oddly, went through what a cat in the capital did.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery-rhyme cat went to London to visit the Queen, so it saw ER (Elizabeth Regina). 'unusually' warns that this word for a carpenter is rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cuts wood with a saw; a rare term for a carpenter or woodworker.

clue.text: Short tunic seen around African city

indicators.note: around means the remaining letters are turned the other way
short means the tunic loses its final letter

parts.note: a tabard is a sleeveless tunic, as worn by heralds

explanation.surface: A cropped garment is spotted somewhere in an African town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the D from TABARD, and 'around' turns TABAR to read RABAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco, in north Africa.

clue.text: By no means religious, from what we hear

indicators.note: this tells the solver the word is identified by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a religious, as a noun, is a monk or nun

explanation.surface: Someone is by no means a believer, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious' looks like an adjective but is the noun for a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, as in 'little the wiser', the word means not at all or in no way.

clue.text: Biblical pop group

definitions.meaning: in the New Testament the Aramaic word for father is used in prayer
the Swedish band that won Eurovision with Waterloo

explanation.surface: A band with a scriptural flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the New Testament Aramaic term for father and the name of a famous Swedish pop quartet.

clue.text: The heartless abuse goes round — it must be suppressed

indicators.note: the abuse is wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: mud is slanderous abuse, as in mud-slinging

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle of the word, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: Cruel slander is circulating and somebody insists it must be silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abuse' as mud comes from mud-slinging, slander thrown at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A muted sound is one that has been softened or subdued, which is to say suppressed.

clue.text: Story covered by English humanist and French dramatist

indicators.note: the story sits inside the humanist's name, which covers it

parts.note: Sir Thomas More, author of Utopia
a story is a lie or fib

explanation.surface: A tale hidden by a Tudor scholar and by a playwright from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the seventeenth-century French playwright of Tartuffe and The Misanthrope.

clue.text: Socialist outside restaurant, revolutionary vandal

indicators.note: revolutionary means the whole is turned round
the socialist goes round the restaurant

parts.note: red is the colour and byword for a socialist
a café is a small restaurant

explanation.surface: A left-winger outside a restaurant turns out to be a radical vandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' seems to describe the socialist, but it turns the whole assembly round, RECAFED to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is someone who disfigures property, spoiling its surface.

clue.text: Where travellers may get off and dance around American street

indicators.note: the dance sits on both sides of the other letters

parts.note: to bop is to dance to pop music

explanation.surface: Passengers alight and start dancing in an American street.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside stopping point where passengers board and leave public buses.

clue.text: Expecting to lose power as monarch

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the expectant word

parts.note: expecting is an idiom for carrying a child
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A pregnant queen may forfeit her authority on the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, so it describes someone ruling as a sovereign.

clue.text: Petition for character behind all others in a situation suggesting crisis

parts.note: to sue is to petition or appeal
Z is the letter that comes after every other one in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A plea made on behalf of the last in line, in what feels like an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1956 Suez Crisis made the canal's name a byword for a political emergency.

clue.text: Ball maybe entertaining any number in the area

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest within

parts.note: Zoe Ball is a British TV and radio presenter; 'maybe' marks her as one example of a Ball
N is the maths symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A dance or party hosting countless guests somewhere nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' suggests a dance or sphere, but it is the surname of broadcaster Zoe Ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is a region or district, so it is a synonym for an area.

clue.text: This remnant has raised objections

indicators.note: raised means read upwards in this down light

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: A leftover piece has been the subject of complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: The short piece left after a cigarette or pencil is used up is a remnant.

clue.text: Music-maker needs key, nothing extra

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A musician needs only a key and nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' points to music, but it is the computer key ALT.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer or an instrument in the range below soprano, so one producing music.

clue.text: Port with a lot of cargo left dumped

indicators.note: dumped means the letter is thrown out

parts.note: laden means heavily loaded

explanation.surface: A ship carrying a heavy load departs after leaving its cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a seaport in Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea.

clue.text: Notice dried crumbs — fatal attraction for mice?

indicators.note: crumbs are broken bits, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sign spotting dried crumbs, the irresistible bait that lures mice to their doom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbs' looks like bait for mice but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Poison bait set to kill vermin is something mice are drawn to that kills them.

clue.text: Always be right in tirade, making noise that echoes around

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed within the tirade

parts.note: a rant is a long angry speech
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to be correct throughout a loud harangue that rings round the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resounding keeps echoing, so its noise rings and reflects back.
